'''Jason Anthoney Richardson Sr.''' (born January 20, 1981) is an American former professional [[basketball]] player who played 14 seasons in the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA). Richardson was taken by the [[Golden State Warriors]] as the fifth overall pick in the [[2001 NBA draft]] after playing [[college basketball]] for the [[Michigan State Spartans men's basketball|Michigan State Spartans]]. Richardson has also played for the [[Charlotte Bobcats]], [[Phoenix Suns]], [[Orlando Magic]], and the [[Philadelphia 76ers]]. Richardson will join the [[Altitude Sports and Entertainment]] television coverage team of the [[Denver Nuggets]] for the upcoming 2026-27 season as a studio analyst.<ref>https://www.9news.com/article/sports/nba/denver-nuggets/new-denver-nuggets-broadcast-team/73-ffc0dec6-2217-4e5b-adc3-f8e0d5538637 {{Bare URL inline|date=September 2026}}</ref>

Richardson is often remembered for his proficiency in dunking and shooting. Early in his career, he won the [[Slam Dunk Contest|NBA Dunk Contest]] in both 2002 and 2003, becoming the second player, after [[Michael Jordan]], to win the competition in consecutive years. Later, he became a more proficient shooter, leading the league in three-pointers made from the 2007–08 to 2011–12 seasons, with 820.<ref>{{cite web |title=Who led nba in total three pointers made from 2007-08 to 2011-12 |url=https://www.statmuse.com/nba/ask?q=who+led+nba+in+total+three+pointers+made+from+2007-08+to+2011-12 |website=statmuse |access-date=11 December 2024 |archive-date=January 20, 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250120105625/https://www.statmuse.com/nba/ask?q=who+led+nba+in+total+three+pointers+made+from+2007-08+to+2011-12 |url-status=live }}</ref> Since 2021, Richardson has been an active player for [[Tri-State (basketball)|Tri-State]] of the [[BIG3]].

==Early life and college==
Born in [[Saginaw, Michigan]], Richardson graduated from [[Arthur Hill High School]] in 1999. Having led the Arthur Hill basketball team to the Class A championship game, Richardson was [[Mr. Basketball of Michigan]] and a McDonald's High School All-American in his senior year. Richardson chose to play college basketball for Michigan State head coach [[Tom Izzo]].

In his [[1999–2000 Michigan State Spartans men's basketball team|freshman season]] at [[Michigan State Spartans men's basketball|Michigan State]], Richardson averaged 5.1 points per game in 37 games (including three starts) and made 50.3% of attempted field goals. Led by [[Mateen Cleaves]] and [[Morris Peterson]], the Spartans won the [[2000 NCAA Men's Division I Basketball Championship Game|NCAA Championship]] with Richardson as a key reserve. In a bigger role in his [[2000–01 Michigan State Spartans men's basketball team|sophomore season]] at Michigan State, he led the Spartans in scoring averaging 14.7 points per game. Richardson played along future NBA players [[Zach Randolph]] and [[Charlie Bell (basketball)|Charlie Bell]] as the Spartans advanced to the [[2001 NCAA Men's Division I Basketball Tournament|Final Four]] before losing to [[2000–01 Arizona Wildcats men's basketball team|Arizona]]. He was named Big Ten First Team that year.<ref name="MSU bio">{{cite web|title=Jason Richardson|url=http://www.msuspartans.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/richardson_jason00.html|publisher=Michigan State Spartans|access-date=June 25, 2011|archive-date=September 26, 2012|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120926193022/http://www.msuspartans.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/richardson_jason00.html|url-status=dead}}</ref>

Richardson graduated from the [[University of Florida]] with his Bachelor of Arts in Sports Management in 2025, the school him and Spartans beat for the 2000 NCAA Men's Basketball National Championship.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://spartanavenue.com/jason-richardson-earns-degree-from-the-school-msu-won-a-national-title-against-01k2akrvwj3a|title=Jason Richardson earns degree from the school MSU won a national title against|date=August 10, 2025|website=Spartan Avenue}}</ref>

==Professional career==

===Golden State Warriors (2001–2007)===
The Warriors drafted Jason Richardson out of Michigan State with the 5th overall pick.

Richardson competed in the [[Rookie Challenge]] as a rookie in 2002 and a sophomore in 2003. His teams won both years, and he was awarded the Rookie Challenge MVP as a rookie. As a sophomore, he had a memorable moment when, in the closing seconds of the game, he bounced the ball off [[Carlos Boozer]]'s forehead and then made a three-pointer before the clock ran out.<ref>[http://static.espn.go.com/nba/allstar/2003/news/2003/0208/1506109.html Warrior tandem score big in loosely-played game] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120116114556/http://static.espn.go.com/nba/allstar/2003/news/2003/0208/1506109.html |date=January 16, 2012 }} February 5, 2003</ref>

During his time with Golden State, Richardson gained popularity for his outstanding scoring, ability to dunk, dedication to the team and fans, and ethical maturity.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.sfgate.com/sports/ostler/article/Richardson-trade-is-good-news-sad-news-2554276.php|title=Richardson trade is good news, sad news|access-date=March 31, 2008|archive-date=October 10, 2007|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20071010080854/http://www.sfgate.com/cgi-bin/article.cgi?f=/c/a/2007/06/29/SPGC8QO8UB1.DTL|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.sfgate.com/cgi-bin/article.cgi?f=/c/a/2007/05/06/SPGUKPM5T01.DTL&hw=jason+richardson&sn=005&sc=758|title=Richardson is being repaid for his loyalty|access-date=October 3, 2008|archive-date=September 20, 2011|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110920080245/http://www.sfgate.com/cgi-bin/article.cgi?f=/c/a/2007/05/06/SPGUKPM5T01.DTL&hw=jason+richardson&sn=005&sc=758|url-status=dead}}</ref> As the long time captain of the Warriors, Richardson organized a letter of apology to Warrior fans in [[2004–05 Golden State Warriors season|2005]] after the team failed to make the playoffs for the 12th straight season. The letter ran in several [[San Francisco Bay Area|Bay Area]] newspapers. The following year, Richardson helped lead the [[2005–06 Golden State Warriors season|Warriors]] to their first playoff trip in 13 years. The Warriors upset the top-seeded [[2005–06 Dallas Mavericks season|Dallas Mavericks]] in the first round, but lost in the second round to the [[2005–06 Utah Jazz season|Utah Jazz]].

Even after leaving Golden State, Richardson remained one of the most popular players among Warrior fans because of his electric style of play and ability to shoot [[three-point field ===Charlotte Bobcats (2007–2008)===
On June 28, 2007, Richardson was traded to the [[Charlotte Bobcats]] along with the draft rights to 36th pick [[Jermareo Davidson]] for the draft rights to eighth pick [[Brandan Wright]].

Richardson began to gain attention with the Bobcats when he led the team to a road win against the [[Boston Celtics]] after scoring 34 points. This was only the Celtics' fourth loss of the season and second loss at home.<ref>[http://www.nba.com/games/20080109/CHABOS/recap.html Richardson, Bobcats Surprise Celtics] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121106191525/http://www.nba.com/games/20080109/CHABOS/recap.html |date=November 6, 2012 }} January 9, 2008</ref> It was also the Bobcats' second road win of the season, ending an 11-game road losing streak. Richardson also led the Bobcats to a franchise-record five consecutive game winning streak, including a home win against his former team, the Golden State Warriors. Richardson posted 42 points against the Warriors.<ref>[http://www.nba.com/games/20080308/CHAWAS/recap.html Richardson's 34 Help Bobcats Bring Down Wizards] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121106191552/http://www.nba.com/games/20080308/CHAWAS/recap.html |date=November 6, 2012 }} March 8, 2008</ref> The [[2007–08 Charlotte Bobcats season|2007–08 season]] was a season of rebuilding for Richardson and the Bobcats. He was able to get his points per game average back up to 21.8, lead the Bobcats in scoring, and lead the league in three-point field goals made.

===Phoenix Suns (2008–2010)===
On December 10, 2008, Richardson was traded along with [[Jared Dudley]], and a 2010 second-round pick to the [[Phoenix Suns]] for [[Boris Diaw]], [[Raja Bell]] and [[Sean Singletary]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Suns Trade for Richardson, Dudley and 2010 Second-Round Pick |work=[[NBA.com]] |url=http://www.nba.com/suns/news/trade_081210.html |access-date=December 11, 2008 |archive-date=November 5, 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121105072004/http://www.nba.com/suns/news/trade_081210.html |url-status=live }}</ref> The Suns dealt for Richardson, as they were looking for another backcourt scorer to take pressure off of [[Steve Nash]].<ref>{{cite news | url=http://archive.boston.com/sports/other_sports/articles/2008/12/11/suns_trade_bell_diaw_for_richardson/ | work=The Boston Globe | title=Suns trade Bell, Diaw for Richardson | date=December 11, 2008 | archive-date=July 30, 2012 | access-date=August 28, 2010 | archive-url=https://archive.today/20120730003454/http://www.boston.com/sports/other_sports/articles/2008/12/11/suns_trade_bell_diaw_for_richardson/ | url-status=live }}</ref>

In his first game as a Sun, Richardson scored a game-high 21 points, including an alley-oop from [[Leandro Barbosa]] that brought the crowd to their feet. His [[2008–09 Phoenix Suns season|first year in Phoenix]] resulted in the team missing the playoffs for the first time since [[2002–03 Phoenix Suns season|2003]].

However, in his [[2009–10 Phoenix Suns season|second year with the team]], he helped bring them back to the playoffs with his play on both the offensive and defensive sides of the ball.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.mlive.com/sports/saginaw/2010/06/jason_richardson_gets_positive.html|title=Jason Richardson gets positive grades after Phoenix Suns season|author=Hugh Bernreuter |date=June 24, 2010|website=mlive}}</ref> In the first round of the [[2010 NBA Playoffs]], Richardson led the Suns to a first-round victory over the [[2009–10 Portland Trail Blazers season|Portland Trail Blazers]],<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.mlive.com/sports/saginaw/2010/04/jason_richardson_leads_phoenix.html|title=Jason Richardson leads Phoenix Suns into second round of NBA Playoffs|author=Hugh Bernreuter |date=April 30, 2010|website=mlive|access-date=September 19, 2025|archive-date=February 22, 2025|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250222101138/https://www.mlive.com/sports/saginaw/2010/04/jason_richardson_leads_phoenix.html|url-status=live}}</ref> including a career playoff-high 42 points in a Game 3 blowout.<ref>{{cite news| url=https://www.foxnews.com/sports/richardson-scores-42-suns-go-up-2-1-over-blazers/ | work=Fox News | title=Richardson scores 42, Suns go up 2–1 over Blazers | date=April 23, 2010}}</ref> In the next round, Richardson helped the Suns to a series sweep against the [[2009–10 San Antonio Spurs season|San Antonio Spurs]], before falling to the [[2009–10 Los Angeles Lakers season|Los Angeles Lakers]] in game 6 of the Western Conference Finals.

===Orlando Magic (2010–2012)===
[[File:J-RichMagic.jpg|thumb|Richardson with the [[Orlando Magic]] in 2010]]
On December 18, 2010, Richardson was traded to the [[Orlando Magic]] along with [[Hedo Türkoğlu]] and [[Earl Clark]] for [[Vince Carter]], [[Marcin Gortat]], [[Mickaël Piétrus]], a 2011 first-round draft pick and $3 million cash.<ref>{{cite web | url=http://www.nba.com/magic/news/news_sunsdeal_121810.html | title=Magic Receive Turkoglu, Richardson & Clark From Suns | work=[[NBA.com]] | date=December 18, 2010 | access-date=December 18, 2010 | archive-date=December 22, 2015 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151222084624/http://www.nba.com/magic/news/news_sunsdeal_121810.html | url-status=live }}</ref>  In December 2011, Richardson agreed to a four-year, $25 million contract to remain in Orlando.<ref>{{cite web|title=Orlando Magic Guard Jason Richardson Guard Surprisingly Resigns|url=http://www.orlandomagic101.com/2011/12/10/orlando-magic-guard-jason-richardson-guard-surprisingly-resigns/|access-date=December 12, 2011|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120426025410/http://www.orlandomagic101.com/2011/12/10/orlando-magic-guard-jason-richardson-guard-surprisingly-resigns/|archive-date=April 26, 2012|url-status=dead}}</ref> The Magic made the playoffs in Richardson's first [[2010–11 Orlando Magic season|year with the team]], losing in the first round to the [[2010–11 Atlanta Hawks season|Atlanta Hawks]].

===Philadelphia 76ers (2012–2015)===
On August 10, 2012, Richardson was traded to the [[Philadelphia 76ers]] in a four-team deal which sent [[Dwight Howard]] to the [[Los Angeles Lakers]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/magic/news/magic-acquire-six-players-five-draft-picks-howard-trade|title=Magic Acquire Six Players, Five Draft Picks in Howard Trade | Orlando Magic|website=www.nba.com|access-date=September 19, 2025|archive-date=June 11, 2025|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250611232312/https://www.nba.com/magic/news/magic-acquire-six-players-five-draft-picks-howard-trade|url-status=live}}</ref> He managed just 33 games in 2012–13 before being ruled out for the rest of the season in January 2013 after undergoing surgery on his left knee, and subsequently sat out the entire 2013–14 season with the injury as well.<ref>{{cite web|last=Zimmerman|first=Kevin|title=Jason Richardson injury likely to sideline him until at least January|date=August 30, 2013 |url=https://www.sbnation.com/nba/2013/8/30/4676698/jason-richardson-injury-knee-sixers|publisher=SB Nation|access-date=April 24, 2014}}</ref>

On February 18, 2015, Richardson was a full participant in practice for the first time in over two years after having not taken to the court in 762 days.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/sixers/news/150219-practice-report|title=J-Rich Returns To Practice; MCW Update; Deadline Day|work=Philadelphia 76ers |access-date=February 19, 2015|archive-date=February 21, 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150221061845/http://www.nba.com/sixers/news/150219-practice-report|url-status=live}}</ref> Two days later, he returned to action for the 76ers as he started against the Indiana Pacers.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/sixers/news/150220-richardson-update|title=Richardson To Start Against Pacers After 25 Months Away |work=Philadelphia 76ers }}</ref> In 18 minutes of play, he recorded 7 points, 7 rebounds, 2 assists, 2 steals and 1 block in the 95–106 loss.<ref>[http://www.nba.com/games/20150220/INDPHI/gameinfo.html Stuckey scores 30 off bench, Pacers beat Sixers 106-95]</ref> On March 4, 2015, he scored a season-high 29 points in a 123–118 overtime loss in Oklahoma City to the Thunder.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400579196|title=Thunder 123-118 76ers (Mar 4, 2015) Game Recap|website=ESPN|access-date=July 17, 2024|archive-date=October 10, 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231010145419/https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400579196|url-status=live}}</ref>

Richardson's final NBA game ever was played on April 11, 2015, in a 107–114 loss to the Chicago Bulls. In that game, Richardson recorded 19 points, 4 rebounds, 2 assists and 1 steal.

===Retirement===
On August 18, 2015, Richardson signed with the [[Atlanta Hawks]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/hawks/news/atlanta-hawks-sign-jason-richardson|title=Atlanta Hawks Sign Jason Richardson|work=NBA.com|publisher=Turner Sports Interactive, Inc.|date=August 18, 2015|access-date=August 18, 2015|archive-date=August 20, 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150820031130/http://www.nba.com/hawks/news/atlanta-hawks-sign-jason-richardson|url-status=live}}</ref> However, less than a month later, Richardson began experiencing pain in his right knee, and an [[MRI]] revealed [[bone spur]]s. On September 23, 2015, he announced his retirement from the NBA, citing he feared that his ability to walk would be impaired for the rest of his life if he continued to play.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://sports.yahoo.com/blogs/nba-ball-dont-lie/jason-richardson-officially-retires-from-nba-after-14-seasons-032500059.html|title=Jason Richardson officially retires from NBA after 14 seasons|work=yahoo.com|date=September 23, 2015|access-date=September 24, 2015|archive-date=September 26, 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150926135531/http://sports.yahoo.com/blogs/nba-ball-dont-lie/jason-richardson-officially-retires-from-nba-after-14-seasons-032500059.html|url-status=live}}</ref>

== Personal life ==
Richardson is the father of Orlando Magic guard [[Jase Richardson]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://msuspartans.com/sports/mens-basketball/roster/jase-richardson/15555|title=Jase Richardson - Men's Basketball|website=Michigan State University Athletics}}</ref> His younger son, Jaxon, is a consensus five-star recruit for the 2026 class. And is committed to play basketball for [[University of Alabama|The University of Alabama]]<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.espn.com/college-sports/basketball/recruiting/player/_/id/255079/jaxon-richardson |access-date=2026-08-17 |website=www.espn.com}}</ref>
